skill.name: testing-skills-with-subagents
skill.description: Test AI skills before deployment with a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR process, pressure scenarios, baseline runs, and rationalization tracking.
skill.summary: Validate AI skills by testing agent behavior before and after the skill is applied.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Static command and filesystem matches are documentation examples, not executable behavior in the skill. The main contextual risk is that the skill recommends deceptive pressure prompts for agent testing, which should stay isolated from live user work.

remediation.issue: Pressure scenarios are framed as real work.
remediation.suggestion: State that scenarios must run only in isolated test sessions and must not trigger live production actions.

remediation.issue: Examples reference the hidden Claude skills directory.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that local skill directory inspection is optional and should not read unrelated hidden files.

remediation.issue: The repository includes a ZIP copy of the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid bundled archives in marketplace submissions, or document that the archive duplicates scanned files.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need proof that agents follow instructions under realistic pressure. This skill provides a repeatable test cycle for baseline failures, fixes, and regression checks.
actual_capabilities: Defines a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR workflow for testing skills.
Shows how to create pressure scenarios with concrete choices.
Guides authors to run baseline tests before writing skill changes.
Explains how to capture agent rationalizations verbatim.
Provides examples for refactoring skills after failed tests.
Includes a complete CLAUDE.md testing example.
limitations: Does not include an automated subagent test harness.
Requires the author to design realistic test scenarios.
Can produce misleading results if scenarios are weak or biased.
Focused on behavior rules, not pure reference documentation.

use_cases.title: Validate a New Skill
use_cases.description: Run baseline and pressure tests before publishing a discipline-focused skill.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Instructions
use_cases.description: Capture agent rationalizations and add targeted counters to close instruction gaps.

use_cases.title: Compare Documentation Variants
use_cases.description: Test multiple instruction styles and compare which version improves agent compliance.
use_cases.target_user: Team leads maintaining Claude or Codex guidance

prompt_templates.title: Start a Baseline Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create three pressure scenarios to test this skill before I revise it.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Rationalizations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failed response and list the exact rationalizations the agent used.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this skill so it directly counters these rationalizations without adding unrelated rules.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Test Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR campaign that compares four documentation variants under repeated pressure tests.

output_examples.input: A skill lets agents skip tests when they are under deadline pressure.
output_examples.output: A test plan with baseline scenarios, expected failures, exact rationalizations, and focused rule changes.

output_examples.input: An agent follows the rule once, then creates a hybrid workaround.
output_examples.output: A refactor plan that adds explicit negations, a rationalization table, and a repeat test.

output_examples.input: A team wants to compare four CLAUDE.md guidance styles.
output_examples.output: A variant matrix that tracks skill discovery, skill use, compliance breaks, and follow-up changes.

best_practices: Run baseline tests before changing the skill.
Use scenarios with at least three realistic pressures.
Record exact agent wording before writing fixes.
anti_patterns: Writing a skill before watching agents fail.
Testing only by asking what the skill says.
Adding broad rules that do not address observed failures.

faq.question: What kind of skills should use this?
faq.answer: Use it for skills that enforce behavior under pressure, such as testing, review, or process discipline.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes a manual testing method and example formats for agent evaluation.

faq.question: Why test without the skill first?
faq.answer: The baseline shows what agents naturally do and which rationalizations the skill must prevent.

faq.question: Can it test reference skills?
faq.answer: It is less useful for pure reference skills because those skills have fewer rules to violate.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: The examples use strong pressure prompts, so authors should run them only in isolated test contexts.
